name: Virtual Desktops
description:
Windows 11 virtual desktops for GNOME, with the same keyboard shortcuts.

• Super+Ctrl+← / → switches to the desktop on the left / right, with a bounce at the first and last one
• Super+Ctrl+D creates a new desktop and switches to it
• Super+Ctrl+F4 closes the current desktop; its windows move to the desktop on the left and stay right where they were
• The desktop's name pops up as you switch, like on Windows 11, and you can rename your desktops
• Desktops stay until you close them, even when they're empty

Every display switches together, like on Windows. The GNOME settings this changes (dynamic workspaces, workspaces on the primary display only) are given back when it's turned off. All shortcuts can be changed.
